alarms.name: First new host after 12 h
alarms.what: The first action, at least 12 hours after the first action, that contacts a host no earlier action named.

alarms.name: First search_for_secrets action
alarms.what: The first action the pack labels search_for_secrets. A pack without that intent never fires it.

alarms.name: Distinct-actor alarm (3 sd, 12 h history)
alarms.what: The first hour with more distinct named actors than the mean plus 3 standard deviations of every earlier hour (at least 12 earlier hours). Known at the end of that hour.

alarms.name: Volume alarm (3 sd, 6 h history)
alarms.what: The first hour with more actions than the mean plus 3 standard deviations of every earlier hour (at least 6 earlier hours). Known at the end of that hour.

variants.name: Volume alarm (3 sd, 12 h history)
variants.what: The volume alarm with 12 hours of history: the baseline published in v2.2.0.

variants.name: First new host after 24 h
variants.what: The new-host alarm after 24 hours of history.

context.key: replay:coordination: one identity carries another's token
context.name: One identity carries another's token

context.name: Two identities share place flb4
First program reused by another actor
First program run by three actors

post_hoc: Post-hoc on one incident: these four alarms were picked as the main early warning after seeing that they fired with more harm still to come than the shared-control signs on the Swarm Traces release. Their thresholds were not tuned, but the choice of alarms (and of the 6 h volume history over the 12 h one) was made with that answer in view, so their figures on that release are not a test.
note: Share of harm still to come = share of the timed harmful records after the alarm. One incident, the one the alarms were picked on. The harm list is the pack's (64% of it dataset commits); see docs/audit-v2.1.md 1.5.
